intro: The detective has vanished, leaving only a violin with one string retuned and a stack of notes addressed to whoever is clever enough to read them. The Irregulars have taken over the room above Baker Street; the fire is low, the tea is bitter, and the mantelpiece is covered in a thin layer of dust that nobody has bothered to wipe. Above the mantel hangs the Irregulars' board of monograms, where every new arrival presses its own single sigil into the wax and leaves it there for the others to find. They work in a comfortable silence, passing the notes from hand to hand, each person adding a line or two to the margins in pencil. Holmes's name is not among them, but the room is full of other marks, waiting for someone to read them the way he would have.
echo: The word once meant the track an animal leaves; now it means whoever follows it.

puzzles.title: Elementary
puzzles.flavor: What the teletype said, before anyone could read it. Unlucky for some, and the same distance either way.

partials.a72b3e08e34b449da3cc64d726aa931704d06aa3: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: Seven positions a row, each punched or not. What were seven bits once enough for? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: Five Orange Pips
puzzles.flavor: Everyone here counts differently. The little number says how. Something in here has been through the looking glass.

partials.954ce6b461a8533ea4ea6a5e6f11834fdc716980: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.

hints: The subscript is a base. Once everything is in ordinary decimal, what range are the numbers in? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.

puzzles.title: The Dog In The Night
puzzles.flavor: The labels matter more than the colours.
hints: Split each colour code into three pairs of hex digits. What else is a two-digit hex number?

puzzles.title: The Reichenbach Fall
puzzles.flavor: Only the first two stripes on each were ever meant to be read.
hints: Engineers read stripes like these as numbers. What number does each part give, and what is a number up to 26?

puzzles.title: The Red-Headed League
puzzles.flavor: Lord Playfair's friend got the credit, but the square is built from whatever is written above it.

blocks.text: HL CA HE TI QL EK RD NC EY EK RT VL NO NH LP BH QH PD KT RH ZM AR BN CP UG HX QH HM PL

hints: An even number of letters, read in pairs, and no pair is ever a double. Which cipher works on pairs, and where's its key?

puzzles.title: A Study In Scarlet
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?

meta.title: Meta: 221B, Upstairs
meta.flavor: Every report is signed with a single initial. Blaise would know what to do with them.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
